šar-ru-ki-in-i₃-lu-ba-ni.draftGloss: Sharrukin-ilubani (Langdon Šar-ru-ki-in-ì-lu-ba-ni) — first king of Agade, Šarrukin, the king known in English as Sargon of Akkad; ŠAR-RU-KI-IN + NI-LU-BA-NI, which Langdon takes as the rest of one name ('Sharrukîn-ilubani'); the copy marks the surface of NI and LU as damaged, and the reading of these last four signs is uncertain

nu-{ĝeš}kiri₆.draftGloss: gardener, orchard-keeper (Langdon nu-giš-šar) — nu, a prefix forming words for a person's trade, + {ĝeš}kiri₆ 'orchard, garden' (GIŠ.SAR; the SAR sign read kiri₆ after the wood sign)

sagi.draftGloss: cup-bearer, a court office — written SAG.ŠU.DUG and read sagi as one word (Langdon reads the signs ka-šu-duĝ); the first sign is taken as SAG from the copy

(sic).draftGloss: a single upright wedge drawn on the copy inside a name and marked 'sic!' by Langdon; not read — a stray or miswritten wedge

ri-mu-uš.draftGloss: Rimush (Langdon Rí-mu-uš) — king of Agade, son of Sargon; RI-MU-UŠ; an Akkadian name

šar-ru-ki-in.draftGloss: Sharrukin (Langdon Šar-ru-ki-in) — Šarrukin, first king of Agade, the king known in English as Sargon of Akkad; ŠAR-RU-KI-IN; an Akkadian name

ma-ni-iš-ti-iš-šu.draftGloss: Manishtishu (Langdon Ma-ni-iš-ti-iš-šu) — king of Agade, son of Sargon and elder brother of Rimush; MA-NI-IŠ-TI-IŠ-ŠU; an Akkadian name, also spelled Ma-ni-iš-te-šu on a Nippur copy

ri-mu-šu-uš.draftGloss: Rimush, miswritten ri-mu-šu-uš (Langdon: 'Sic! Error for Ri-mu-uš-šu') — the king of Agade, son of Sargon, named as Manishtishu's younger brother; the last two signs are in the wrong order

na-ra-am-{d}suen.draftGloss: Naram-Suen (Langdon Narâm-Sin, Na-ra-am-ᵈEn-zu) — king of Agade, son of Manishtishu; NA-RA-AM + the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU, Langdon Sin) with the divine determinative; an Akkadian name; on this prism the god's name and the following line are largely restored by Langdon

šar-ga-li₂-šar-ri.draftGloss: Shargalisharri (Langdon Šar-ga-lí-šar-rí) — king of Agade, son of Naram-Suen; ŠAR-GA-LI₂-ŠAR-RI (li₂ the NI sign); an Akkadian name; on this prism only the first sign survives, damaged, and the rest is Langdon's restoration from a Nippur copy

a-ba.draftGloss: who? — interrogative pronoun; a-ba-am₃ 'who is it / who was it?'

nu.draftGloss: not — negative particle (the NU sign); before a noun, 'not (a) …'

i-gi₄-gi₄.draftGloss: Igigi (Langdon [I-gí-]gí) — a king of Agade, the first of four named after 'who was king? who was not king?'; I-GI₄-GI₄, the beginning restored by Langdon; other copies have ì-gi-gi and ì-ki-ki

i-mi.draftGloss: Imi (Langdon [I-mi]) — a king of Agade, one of four named after 'who was king?'; on this prism the name is in a break and is restored by Langdon from other copies

na-ni.draftGloss: Nani (Langdon [Na-ni]) — a king of Agade, one of four named after 'who was king?'; on this prism the name is in a break and is restored by Langdon; other copies have na-nu-um

du-du.draftGloss: Dudu (Langdon Du-du) — king of Agade, father of Shu-Durul; DU-DU

šu-dur-ulₓ.draftGloss: Shu-Durul (Langdon Gimil-dur-ūl) — king of Agade, son of Dudu; ŠU (Langdon's Gimil, read šu by sign) + DUR + KIB, which Langdon (after Scheil) reads ul; the name is in a break on this prism and the signs shown are Langdon's restoration; the reading of the last sign is uncertain
